 Google brings back App Lock for Pixel, with a wide release set for Q1 2027 
 Once an app is locked, all the notification content will remain hidden. Recent app previews are redacted, and its widgets and shortcuts are removed until you authenticate again. 
 By
 Anvinraj Valiyathara 
 Published November 18, 2026 7:55 PM 
 Save 
 Vikhyaat Vivek / Digital Trends 
 When Google rolled out the Android 17 QPR2 beta back in August, it included a new App Lock feature for Pixel phones. The privacy-focused feature let users lock apps behind biometric or PIN authentication. While it was a nifty feature, it disappeared from the subsequent updates. It made a comeback in QPR3 Beta 3 in October, and Google is now inviting Pixel beta testers to try it again, saying it should ship with the QPR3 platform release in Q1 2027.
 How do you lock an app using the App Lock?
 Google 
 On a Pixel phone running the QPR3 Beta, you can long-press an app icon on the home screen or in the app drawer and choose App Lock. You will need to confirm with your PIN, pattern, password, fingerprint, or face unlock. You can also manage several locks at once in Settings under Security & privacy and then App Lock.
 Recommended Videos 
 Once an app is locked, all the notification content will remain hidden. Recent app previews are redacted, and its widgets and shortcuts are removed until you authenticate again. A locked app’s icon doesn’t change, so anyone looking at your phone can’t tell which apps you’ve locked.
 App Lock is unavailable for certain preloaded apps and for apps that hold specific system roles. If you’ve allowed AI agents and services to access a locked app, they can still reach its data. Photos and videos stored in a locked app may still appear in other apps that already have access to them. Google recommends Private Space if you want stronger protection than a simple app lock.
 When can you get App Lock on your Pixel?
 For now, the App Lock feature is available to Pixel users running the QPR3 Beta. If you would rather not run beta software, you will need to wait a little longer for it. Once the beta testing wraps up, it should reach everyone with the stable QPR3 release in Q1 2027. Until then, Android 17 already has other security tools worth turning on, along with fresh features from the November Pixel Drop .
 App Lock isn’t limited to Pixel phones either, since Samsung is rolling out its native version in the One UI 9.5 beta , which opened on November 18 for Galaxy S26 phones. The feature is built into Android 17 QPR2, which appears to be the foundation for One UI 9.5. Other Android phone makers haven’t announced their plans yet, but App Lock should reach more devices once they adopt the newer Android 17 builds.

 Anonymous messaging apps may not be as private as you think 
 Your burner account and your family group chat have more in common than you think. 
 If you think that having a separate app for your friends and family and an anonymous chat app for talking to strangers can keep your identity secret, think again. Researchers from the University of Maryland and KAIST have just shown how quickly those two lives get stitched back together.
 Their study was presented at the 2026 Network and Distributed System Security Symposium, and it covered KakaoTalk, Telegram, WhatsApp, Signal, and Tinder. The team didn’t use any hacking or encryption-breaking methods.

 A smartphone camera could help doctors identify diabetic foot ulcers that won’t heal 
 One photo, no touching, and a clip-on camera that tells your doctor when a wound is heading for trouble. 
 Over 500 million people in the world are affected by diabetes, and about one-third of them are going to develop foot ulcers sooner or later. The current system uses a four-week treatment and follow-up protocol to determine whether the ulcer is healing. 
 But if people are not careful about their hospital visits, the ulcer can get worse quietly, can result in a serious infection, or even result in amputation. Yet the standard of care still asks everyone to wait.

 Google wants all apps to be foldable-ready, and the shift goes into effect next year 
 Google Play is finally tired of apps that waste your foldable's screen 
 Google is introducing new adaptive quality rules on Google Play to make apps work seamlessly on foldables and other large screens. Starting in April 2027, apps will need to meet at least the baseline Tier 3 standard for foldables. Those that miss the bar will no longer be able to publish or update and may get less visibility in the store. Existing apps that never get an update will remain downloadable.
 Google says more than 580 million large-screen devices are already in use, from tablets and Googlebook laptops to Android XR devices. If you have ever unfolded a phone only to find a letterboxed app in the middle of the display, this is the change meant to stop it.
